## Why This Is Asked

- DNS resolution paths and final A records
- Split-horizon DNS and authoritative servers
- TLS SNI handling at CDN/edge

```bash
# Track DNS path
dig +trace api.internal.example

# Validate TLS with explicit SNI and IP mapping
curl -I --resolve api.internal.example:443:IP https://api.internal.example

```

- What changes would you propose if split-horizon DNS is confirmed?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to diagnose cross-region telemetry jitter with a mixed failure surface (clock, queues, MTU, timers) using real tools.

## Key Concepts

- Clock synchronization: NTP/PTP/chrony/ptp4l
- Linux networking: tc qdisc, VXLAN MTU, path MTU discovery
- Tracing: mtr, ping -M do
- Telemetry path design: cross-region edge mesh

## Code Example

```javascript
# Time sync checks
ntpq -p
chronyc tracking
# Queue inspection
tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
# Path MTU test
ping -M do -s 1472 cross-region-host
# Tracer
mtr -rwzlc 100 cross-region-host
```

## Follow-up Questions

- If skew dominates, how would you re-architect clocking?
- If MTU fragmentation is the issue, what changes would you apply to VXLAN and path MTU discovery?
